# 2 Kings Chapter 24 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 244v–245r

---

**24:1** In-his-days went-up Nevukhadnetstsar [Nebuchadnezzar] king of-Bavel, and-became Yehoyaqim his-servant [le-'eved lo] three years. And-he-turned and-rebelled [vayimrod] against-him.

**24:2** And-sent YHWH against-him bands [gedudey] of-Kasdim [Chaldeans] and-bands of-Aram and-bands of-Mo'av and-bands of-the-sons of-Ammon. And-he-sent-them against Yehudah to-destroy-it [le-ha'avido], according-to-the-word of-YHWH which he-spoke by-the-hand of-his-servants the-prophets.

**24:3** Surely [akh] by-the-command [al pi] of-YHWH it-was against Yehudah, to-remove [le-hasir] from-his-face [me-'al panayv], on-account-of the-sins of-Menasheh, according-to-all which he-did.

**24:4** And-also [ve-gam] the-innocent blood [dam ha-naqi] which he-shed, and-he-filled Yerushalayim [with] innocent blood, and-YHWH was-not willing [lo avah] to-forgive [li-slo'ach].

**24:5** And-the-rest of-the-acts of-Yehoyaqim and-all which he-did, are-they-not written in-the-book of-the-chronicles of-the-kings of-Yehudah?

**24:6** And-lay-down Yehoyaqim with his-fathers, and-reigned Yehoyakhin his-son in-his-place.

**24:7** And-did-not add [lo yosaf] again the-king of-Mitsrayim to-come-out from-his-land, for the-king of-Bavel had-taken, from-the-Wadi of-Mitsrayim [nachal Mitsrayim] to the-river Perat [Euphrates], all which had-been [belonging] to-the-king of-Mitsrayim.

**24:8** A-son of-eighteen years [was] Yehoyakhin when-he-became-king, and-three months he-reigned in-Yerushalayim. And-the-name of-his-mother [was] Nechushta daughter of-Elnatan from-Yerushalayim.

**24:9** And-he-did the-evil in-the-eyes of-YHWH, according-to-all which his-father had-done.

**24:10** In-that time went-up the-servants of-Nevukhadnetstsar king of-Bavel to-Yerushalayim, and-the-city came under-siege [ba-matsur].

**24:11** And-came Nevukhadnetstsar king of-Bavel against the-city, and-his-servants [were] besieging-it [tsarim 'aleyha].

**24:12** And-went-out [vayetse] Yehoyakhin king of-Yehudah to the-king of-Bavel, he and-his-mother and-his-servants and-his-officers [sarisayv] and-his-officials [sarayv]. And-took-him [vayiqqach oto] the-king of-Bavel in-the-eighth year of-his-reign [le-molkho].

**24:13** And-he-brought-out from-there all the-treasures [otserot] of-the-house of-YHWH and-the-treasures of-the-house of-the-king, and-he-cut-in-pieces [vayeqatstsets] all the-vessels of-gold which Shelomoh king of-Yisra'el had-made in-the-temple [heykhal] of-YHWH, as YHWH had-spoken.

**24:14** And-he-exiled [ve-heglah] all Yerushalayim, and-all the-officers [ha-sarim] and-all the-mighty-warriors [gibborey ha-chayil], ten-thousand [aseret alafim] exiles [goleh], and-all the-craftsmen [ha-charash] and-the-smiths [ha-masger]. None remained [lo nish'ar] except the-poorest of-the-people of-the-land [dallat 'am ha-arets].

**24:15** And-he-exiled Yehoyakhin to-Bavel, and-the-mother of-the-king and-the-wives of-the-king and-his-officers and-the-mighty-ones of-the-land [eyley ha-arets], he-led [holikh] into-exile [golah] from-Yerushalayim to-Bavel.

**24:16** And-all the-men of-might [anshey ha-chayil], seven-thousand, and-the-craftsmen and-the-smiths, one-thousand, all [of them] mighty-warriors [gibborim] — doers of-war [osey milchamah] — and-brought-them the-king of-Bavel into-exile to-Bavel.

**24:17** And-made-king the-king of-Bavel Mattanyah his-uncle [dodo] in-his-place, and-he-turned [vayyassev] his-name to-Tsidqiyyahu.

**24:18** A-son of-twenty and-one years [was] Tsidqiyyahu when-he-became-king, and-eleven years he-reigned in-Yerushalayim. And-the-name of-his-mother [was] Chamutal daughter of-Yirmeyahu from-Livnah.

**24:19** And-he-did the-evil in-the-eyes of-YHWH, according-to-all which Yehoyaqim had-done.

**24:20** For on-account-of the-anger [af] of-YHWH it-came-about in-Yerushalayim and-Yehudah, until he-cast-them [hishlikho] from his-face [me-'al panayv]. And-rebelled [vayimrod] Tsidqiyyahu against the-king of-Bavel.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.2 — "YHWH sent against him bands":** The narrator attributes the raiding bands of Chaldeans, Arameans, Moabites, and Ammonites directly to YHWH's agency. Political and military events are theological events.

**v.4 — "YHWH was not willing to forgive":** The Hebrew *lo avah YHWH li-slo'ach* is one of the starkest theological statements in the Hebrew Bible. The verb *salachh* (forgive) is used exclusively of God in the OT. Here, divine forgiveness is explicitly refused.

**v.13 — "cut in pieces all the vessels of gold":** The systematic dismantling of Solomon's temple vessels — crafted with extraordinary artistry (1 Kings 7) — is narrated with clinical precision. What took chapters to build is destroyed in a clause.

**v.14 — "except the poorest of the people of the land":** The phrase *dallat 'am ha-arets* (the poorest of the people of the land) describes those left behind — the economically insignificant. Babylon took the elite; the dregs remained.

*— EMET*
